name: Teneligliptin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Teneligliptin is a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor cleared by both liver (CYP3A4, flavin monooxygenases) and kidney (15% to 22% unchanged in urine). Kidney impairment raises exposure only modestly (at most about 1.7-fold), and the Thai label, based on the Japanese originator, sets no kidney dose adjustment; hemodialysis removes about 16% of a dose. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The label reports kidney pharmacokinetics by severity without numeric thresholds or dose changes; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual: 20 mg once daily; may increase to 40 mg once daily with close monitoring (Thai SmPC).

The label gives no kidney dose change; exposure (AUC) was about 1.25-, 1.68- and 1.49-fold higher in mild, moderate and severe impairment (Thai SmPC). A dedicated PK study found no need for adjustment through end-stage kidney disease (Halabi 2013). The 40 mg dose was not studied in kidney impairment; increase only with close monitoring.

hd.text: No dose change in the label; end-stage kidney failure AUC about 1.16-fold; hemodialysis removed 15.6% of the dose (Thai SmPC). Dialysis timing not critical.

pd.text: No PD data; no change expected from end-stage kidney failure data (AUC about 1.16-fold).
pd.short: No PD data; likely no change

crrt.text: No data. Insulin is usual in critical illness.

dialyzable: Partly: hemodialysis removed 15.6% of the dose (Thai SmPC).
monitoring: Hypoglycemia with a sulfonylurea or insulin (lower their dose). Avoid with QT prolongation or torsades history; caution with class IA or III antiarrhythmics. Persistent severe abdominal pain (pancreatitis), intestinal obstruction in those with prior abdominal surgery (Thai SmPC). Caution in severe hepatic impairment (no experience). In dialysis patients, check QTc and electrolytes when other QT risk factors are present.
